cue_text: Blast lesions (Magnaporthe oryzae) are spindle-shaped -- pointed at both ends like a narrow eye or diamond -- with a grey-to-whitish centre and a dark brown margin. Brown spot lesions (Helminthosporium oryzae / Bipolaris oryzae) are cylindrical to oval, not pointed, dark brown, usually ringed by a yellow halo. Lesion shape is the more reliable single field to ask about: colour (grey centre vs. yellow halo) can be harder to judge under variable light and lesion age than the pointed-vs-rounded outline. Source: TNAU Agritech Portal, Crop Protection > Rice Diseases -- 'Blast: Magnaporthe oryzae' (agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_protection/rice_diseases/rice_1.html) and 'Rice Brown Spot or Sesame Leaf Spot: Helminthosporium oryzae' (rice_2.html), accessed 2026-08-31. Corroborated by IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank, 'Blast (leaf and collar)' fact sheet: leaf blast lesions are 'elongated and pointed at each end,' brown spot lesions 'tend to be more round.'
question_text: Look closely at one of the spots on the leaf. Is it pointed at both ends, like a narrow diamond or an eye shape, rather than round or oval?

cue_text: Both bore into squares/bolls and leave round holes with damaged seeds and lint — the entry damage alone doesn't tell them apart.
question_text: Cut open the damaged boll — are the larvae inside pink or rose-colored?

cue_text: Both cause leaf yellowing, curling and distortion on young growth — the curling shape alone doesn't distinguish sap-suckers from thrips scarring.
question_text: Is the leaf surface sticky, or coated with a black sooty growth?

cue_text: Whitefly is the vector for cotton leaf curl virus, so both a live infestation and an established viral infection can show leaf curling on the same plant — the curl shape doesn't say which is the active problem.
question_text: Tap the leaf — do small white insects fly up from the underside?

cue_text: Both distort and curl young leaves — thrips scarring and viral vein-thickening can look similar in a single top-down photo.
question_text: Turn the leaf over — are there small leaf-like outgrowths (enations) along the veins?

cue_text: Both progress to blackening and plant death — a photo of a wilted, dying plant late in the disease doesn't show which one started it.
question_text: Are there angular, water-soaked spots visible on the leaves?

cue_text: Pink bollworm causes poor boll opening; bacterial blight causes boll rot — both can leave a boll looking damaged and discolored from outside.
question_text: Does the boll have black, water-soaked lesions on its surface?
